findings.evidence: check-bump.sh:201-202 vs lean_versions.py:14 `RELEASE_RE`, :75-86 `release_refs`, :94-98 `release_tags`; resolve_deps.py:172 and toolchain_tags.py:221 are the two existing consumers of `release_tags`.
findings.fix: Put "which release tag, restricted to the v4 ruleset, does this sha carry" in lean_versions.py next to `why_not_newer` (reusing `parse_release`/`release_refs`, with the v4 restriction as the shared parameter) and have check-bump.sh ask it through the same `sys.path.insert` heredoc it already uses for `cache_source`, with `resolve_deps.release_tags` reading the same restriction.
findings.issue: The release-tag test re-implements `lean_versions.release_tags`/`release_refs` (its own `repos/$SLUG/tags?per_page=100 --paginate` listing) and restates `lean_versions.RELEASE_RE` as an inline grep `^v4\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-rc[0-9]+)?$`. lean_versions.py:3-5 states this rule lives there once precisely so the resolver cannot propose a pin the guard rejects; the two copies already disagree in scope — `release_refs` keeps any `vX.Y.Z[-rcN]`, so `resolve_deps.forward` returns "release" (resolve_deps.py:306, `self.tags` from lean_versions.release_tags at resolve_deps.py:172) for a tag the guard's `v4`-only grep refuses (test_check_bump.py:254 `test_only_v4_tags_count_as_releases`).

findings.evidence: check-bump.sh:197 `ML_TC_NEW="$(gh api "repos/$SLUG/contents/lean-toolchain?ref=$REV_P" ...)"` and check-bump.sh:301 `ML_TC="$(gh api "repos/$ML_SLUG/contents/lean-toolchain?ref=$ML_REV_P" ...)"`; line 177 sets `ML_SLUG="$SLUG"; ML_REV_P="$REV_P"` for mathlib.
findings.fix: Reuse the value already held: `ML_TC="${ML_TC_NEW:-$(gh api ... )}"` (ML_TC_NEW is set only on mathlib's diverged path, so the fetch still happens otherwise), and extend `test_the_guard_asks_master_membership_once` to assert the toolchain path is requested once too.
findings.issue: In the diverged-mathlib path the same `gh api repos/$SLUG/contents/lean-toolchain?ref=$REV_P` is issued twice: line 197 stores it in `ML_TC_NEW`, line 301 fetches the identical path again into `ML_TC` (`ML_SLUG`/`ML_REV_P` are that same slug and rev, set at line 177). This is the same redundancy the PR removed for the master-membership compare, where the answer is plumbed through as `known_on_master` (line 243) and asserted by test_check_bump.py:239-245.

summary: Both prior findings are fixed (step 2b now calls mathlib_cache.cache_source with the compare answer plumbed in; resolve_deps.forward reads lean_versions.toolchain_order). Remaining: the guard hand-rolls the release-tag listing and release-name regex that lean_versions already owns, and re-fetches mathlib's lean-toolchain it already holds.
